Official statement from @Tesla regarding Cybertruck PCS failures.

- If you paid out of pocket, you'll receive a refund/reimbursement.

- Extended warranties on the part.

- Vehicles receive free supercharging if waiting for a part replacement.

More details in quoted post.


Cybertruck (@cybertruck)

We've identified PCS electronics in pre-2026 Cybertrucks that do not meet our reliability standards and have made design changes to address this in newer vehicles.

Next steps for existing owners:
– Model year 2026: PCS warranty is now standard at 7 years/70k miles
– Model year 2024/2025: PCS warranty extended to 8 years/150k miles

Starting in the next few weeks, we will reimburse any charges for those who already required a PCS replacement and paid out of pocket.

We're working hard on increasing supply chain availability of this improved version.

As an immediate remedy, we've rolled out a software update so you can keep Supercharging even if a PCS failure occurs, and have enabled free Supercharging for trucks waiting for part availability

Earlier we identified an issue with Groups not being accessible by its own members thanks to a report by @AusTeslaOwners.

This resulted from related optimizations we made to our API backend yesterday and has now been resolved.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused by this.

We're adding what countries are included in a new Tesla software wave to help provide much needed context.

When available, we'll also include additional details in a subsequent reply post, such as what software versions vehicles are originating from.

Your feedback matters.
